Its where argument picks rows by a column's value, such as the Company column eq Stripe, with match any when several values will do, scope first_n takes the first few, and dry_run prices the run first when the person asked what it would cost. preview_export_column renders what a row would send without writing anything, for checking a mapping before it runs. A field's value can be a column, one part of a column ('Research › city'), or text combined with columns in double braces ('{{Title}} at {{Company}}'), as the setup's value picker offers. fixed_values writes the same text into a field of every record, after_column places it, and the options rows set how it writes, what the column editor offers:
- update_mode (one of patch, replace, set_once): How an update writes: patch changes only the mapped fields (the default), replace overwrites the whole record, set_once writes only where the destination is empty.
- remove_blanks (yes or no): yes leaves a field out when its value is empty (the default); no sends the blank, which clears that value at the destination.
- typecast (yes or no): yes converts each value to the destination field's type first (the default); no sends it as written.
- only_on_change (yes or no): yes skips a row whose values are the ones last written (the default); no writes every row on every run.
- batched (yes or no): yes writes rows in batches: faster, but the receipts say pushed rather than created or updated. no by default.
- retry_on_failure (yes or no): yes retries a row that failed on a rate limit, a server error or the network (the default); no leaves it failed, as max_retries 0 does.
- max_retries (a whole number): Retries per row beyond the first, 0 to 10; 3 by default. 0 turns retrying off, as the setup's Retries box does.
- timeout_seconds (a whole number): Seconds to wait for the destination on each request, 1 to 600.
- requests_per_minute (a whole number): The most writes a minute, 1 to 6000; the destination's own pace by default.
update_export_column changes any of it later. Free to add.

table_id.description: The table whose rows would be pushed.

column_name.description: What to call the column. The cells hold the RECEIPT of each push, never the row's own data, so name it for the destination: 'Pushed to HubSpot'. (maxLength: 255)

integration.description: The destination, by name or id, from list_export_destinations.

record_type.description: The destination object to write, such as contacts, spelled as it lists it.

action.description: What each row does at the destination. upsert updates a matching record and creates one otherwise, create never touches an existing record, update never makes a new one. (default: 'upsert')

match_on.description: How a row is matched to a record over there, as 'destination field=Column name' pairs, for example 'email=Work email'. Several are an ordered FALLBACK, not a composite key: the first that has a value for a row is the one that row is matched on. A row whose match value is empty is skipped rather than written. Match people on an email field and an email column, and companies on their domain and a website column, as the setup starts them: never on a name, a description, an id the table does not hold, a flag or a date, which would update whichever record shares it. With neither, ask the person what to match on. The column can be one part of a column that holds several values, as the setup's picker shows it: 'Column › part', a field an AI column answers with (get_table lists its outputs) or a list's item by its place from 0 ('Competitors › 0'). Up to 25 pairs; the rest are dropped.

field_mappings.description: What to write, as 'destination field=Column name' pairs, for example 'firstname=First name'. The value is a column, one part of one ('city=Company research › city'), or the setup's Combine columns or type a value…: typed text with each column in double braces, 'jobtitle={{Title}} at {{Company}}', which is sent as text. At least one is required. Up to 25 pairs; the rest are dropped.

fixed_values.description: Destination fields written with the same text on every record, as 'destination field=text' pairs: 'lead_source=Oneprofile'. (maxItems: 25)

after_column.description: The column to place it after, by name. Leave empty for the end. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

options.description: More export settings, one row each: option and value. The options are update_mode, remove_blanks, typecast, only_on_change, batched, retry_on_failure, max_retries, timeout_seconds, requests_per_minute. Leave empty for the usual behavior. (maxItems: 20)

OptionRow.description: One setting given as a row: which option, and its value in words or digits.

option.description: The option's name, exactly as the option list prints it.

value.description: Its value: a number as digits, yes or no, one of the option's choices, or text. A list is written with commas between its items. (default: '')

tools.name: preview_export_column
tools.description: Dry run an export column against real rows: render exactly what each row would send, ask the destination read only whether the row already matches a record, and report whether a real run would create, update or skip it, over the rows at the top of the table or the ones a where filter picks. NOTHING IS WRITTEN, and the writing half of the export is not reachable from this path at all. Do this before anybody runs an export, because a mapping that looks right and a mapping that is right read the same on a card. Free.

table_id.description: The table the export column sits on.

column_name.description: The export column, named as the table names it.

row_count.description: How many rows to render, from the top of the table. (minimum: 1; maximum: 10; default: 5)

where.description: Dry run only the rows that meet every one of these conditions, as read_table_rows takes them: 'preview the push for the Won rows'. Leave empty for the rows at the top of the table. (maxItems: 20)

one_row_per.description: A column, by name: of the rows where keeps, only the first of each value in it, as read_table_rows takes it. Blank rows stay in. (default: '')

RowFilterArg.description: One condition a row has to satisfy.

column.description: Column name or 'Column › Field'; 'any column' with has_error or has_no_error asks the whole row.

operator.description: has_error, has_results, has_not_run, is_stale and run_stopped ask what a cell's last run DID; has_error also finds a bad email or link. The rest: what it HOLDS.

value.description: Text, read as a number or true/false against such a column. Empty for operators taking none (is_empty, is_true, has_error and the run-state family). The _any_of ones: alternatives separated by commas, one holding a comma in double quotes; (empty) is blank cells. (default: '')

joiner.description: or: any condition at its level may hold; and: all. (default: 'and')

group.description: Conditions sharing 1, 2... are bracketed. (minimum: 0; maximum: 8; default: 0)

tools.name: get_export_column_summary
tools.description: Say where an export column sends and count what it has actually pushed: the object, the tool and the connection it writes to, its match and its fields to send by the tool's own labels (or, on a sandbox copy, that it sends nowhere until a tool is picked), then how many rows were created at the destination, how many updated, and when the newest push happened. The answer to 'where does it send' and 'did it work'; never guess a destination from a column's name. It counts what the destination confirmed, so a row missing from the count was skipped or failed rather than quietly written. Free.

table_id.description: The table the export column sits on.

column_name.description: The export column, named as the table names it.

tools.name: write_sequence_previews
tools.description: Write every step's message for several contacts of a sequence at once, up to ten, and show them all: for each contact the agent writes their whole thread the way the real first send does, a step a person wrote is filled in from their row, and the answer carries each contact's subject and words in the order they send, with a link to that contact's thread in the sequence's Preview. Call it straight after build_sequence builds a sequence on a table, and show the person what it answers. Call it too when somebody asks to see the emails a sequence would send, rather than previewing one contact and one step at a time. Leave record_ids empty to take the first contacts the sequence can reach; a contact it cannot reach (no address for its channels, in another sequence, on Do not contact, reached too recently) is never written for, and the answer names them with why. It sends nothing and costs no credits; each message the agent writes counts against the workspace's daily preview allowance, and a contact written for before is read back at no cost. Each thread is kept on the sequence's Preview as written, so the link shows the same words and the person can mark it Looks good there. The real send is written fresh at send time unless the thread is marked Looks good, which makes it what sends. A thread already written is shown as it was saved, and the answer says so, unless write_again asks for it to be written fresh; a saved thread from before the plain-words check that uses banned jargon or copies the business context is written again once either way. read_sequence_previews reads back what is already written.

record_ids.description: The contacts, by row id in the audience table, up to ten. Empty takes the first ones the sequence can reach, in the order added; one it cannot reach is never written for. (maxItems: 10)

contacts.description: How many reachable contacts to write for when record_ids is empty. Every one up to ten unless the person asked for fewer. (minimum: 1; maximum: 10; default: 10)

write_again.description: True when the person asks for the emails written again: each thread is written fresh. A thread marked Looks good is kept, since it is what sends. False shows what is written and writes only what is not. (default: False)

tools.name: send_test_email
tools.description: Send one step as a REAL email to a real inbox, rendered for one contact: the sequence's own mailbox, the real signature, the variables resolved. Leave to_address empty and it goes to the person running this conversation, which is what 'send me a test' means, and leave mailbox_id empty and it leaves from the first connected mailbox of the sequence's senders. The contact whose row it renders is not written to and learns nothing. It costs no credits and is left out of the sequence's analytics, and it does not launch the sequence or enrol anybody. It is still an email arriving in somebody's inbox, so it always asks a person first. An agent written step is written fresh for the test the way a preview is, together with the rest of the sequence for a contact not written to yet, from the same free daily budget a preview draws on, each step written counting, which makes a test of one a sample rather than the email that arrives. Agent words the real send would hold for a person (stray markup, a placeholder) are refused with the reasons and no test goes out: pass the reasons on, and offer to fix the message or test another contact. The step is named by its step id or its message number, both printed by get_sequence.

sequence_id.description: The sequence, by the id from get_sequence.

step_id.description: The step, by the step id from get_sequence, which prints it on every step. Give this or message_number. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

message_number.description: Instead of step_id: which message of the cadence, counting from 1 among the steps that carry words, as get_sequence prints '(message 2, ...)'.

record_id.description: The contact the variables render against, which is the id of their row in the audience table. Nothing is sent to them.

to_address.description: Where the test goes. Leave it empty to send it to the person running this conversation, which is what 'send me a test' means. (maxLength: 320; default: '')

mailbox_id.description: Which mailbox it really leaves from. Leave it empty to use the first connected mailbox of the sequence's own senders, which is the one the real send would use. (default: '')

tools.name: list_senders
tools.description: List who this workspace can send as: each sender's name, how many mailboxes it holds, how many emails it has sent today against what it may send, its send mode (Send when confident, Always ask or Always send, which says how much of what the agent writes goes out without a person), its job title and booking link, its timezone and where it came from (chosen by a person, detected from its LinkedIn browser, or a guess), whose midnight resets its daily limits and whose hours its sequences send in, its signature (trimmed here, whole when one sender is read), and the LinkedIn identity paired with it with today's connection requests against the cap. Give profile_id to read one sender on its own, which is the read to take before changing a signature. This is where every other tool in this family gets its ids. A sender with no mailbox is a draft and sends nothing, which the answer says. It does not read the mailboxes themselves, and it does not read a sender's LinkedIn ceilings: get_sender_linkedin does that. Free, and it changes nothing.

search.description: Only senders whose name matches this text. Leave empty for all of them. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

profile_id.description: One sender's id, to read that sender on its own with everything the listing knows about it. Leave empty to list them all. (default: '')

tools.name: list_approval_queue
tools.description: Read what is waiting on a person: the drafted emails and LinkedIn steps a sender's rule holds back until a human says yes, with who each goes to (name, address or LinkedIn profile, and domain), the contact's title and company, the sequence, the step, how long each has been waiting, the subject a reply in an existing thread goes out with, and the first lines of the message. Narrow to one type of step with task_types ('only the connection requests'). A message the agent wrote also says how sure the agent was (its word and a score out of 100), whether a check flagged its words (leave those out of an approval by score), and why it is waiting instead of sending, in words. Narrow to one recipient with to, or leave one out with not_to, by name, address or domain: that is how 'approve all the drafts except the one to Melanie' is done, by listing with not_to and passing the ids that come back straight to approve_tasks in the same reply. Narrow to one contact by their audience row with record_id. Narrow by why a task waits with ask_reason, and by words in the contact or the subject with search, as the Tasks page's Why it needs approval and search box do: the queue applies both, so they reach every task. Narrow by score with min_confidence and max_confidence; like to, these are applied over the page read, and the answer says how far that reached. Read it in any order the page's columns sort by with order: newest first (as the page opens), oldest first ('what has waited longest'), or by contact A to Z or Z to A. It also carries the count for the whole workspace, so 'how much is waiting' is answered even when the rows are narrowed. A pending LinkedIn row says whether a browser is open for its sender, so whether it would run soon once approved. A row with unsaved_feedback is the page's Unsaved feedback: notes in the card's Feedback column whose changes wait (read_needs_work reads it). show reads each place the Tasks page lists: 'approved' is approved work not yet gone, the Pending tab, each row saying where its work stands (queued, how many are ahead and when it is expected to start, running, waiting for the sending window to open in its sender's timezone); 'open' is Open and Pending together, waiting and approved; 'decided' is the history on Completed, what was sent, refused or cancelled, and 'everything' every tab, which is how a task somebody already approved or refused is looked up. Set show to 'failed' for the steps that could not be done, which is the answer to 'which LinkedIn steps failed': each says why, whether its contact can be retried, and the sequence_id and contact_id change_contact_journeys retries it by, with action retry. Tasks is what was asked of a person; what went out as a sender, with who let each go (approved, automatic with nobody asked, rejected, sent by a person from the inbox), every email and inbox reply beside the LinkedIn steps, is Activity, the Tasks page's Completed tab: list_sender_activity. It decides nothing by itself. Free.

show.description: Which tasks to read. The Tasks page has three tabs: Open, what waits on a person; Pending, what was approved and waits on its channel; and Completed, what went out or was refused. 'waiting' is the queue itself, the Open tab: everything waiting on a person right now (Needs approval). 'approved' is the Pending tab: work let go, by a person or a rule, still waiting on its channel (Approved), each row saying where its work stands. 'open' is waiting and approved together, which no one tab lists. 'decided' is the history on Completed: everything already sent, refused or cancelled (Done, Rejected, Cancelled, Failed, a LinkedIn step's Skipped or Stopped). A task the agent is writing again (Writing) stays where it was in 'waiting' and 'open' until it comes back with the new words; it reads cancelled meanwhile, so 'decided' lists it too. 'failed' is the steps that could not be done (Failed), Completed's Failed outcome, each saying why and whether its contact can be retried. 'everything' is every task on every tab. (default: 'waiting')

channel.description: Only this channel's tasks. 'browser' is the Needs human tasks Browser use runs leave. 'any' reads every channel together. (default: 'any')

sequence_id.description: Only tasks from this sequence, by id from get_sequence. Empty for all. (default: '')

sender_profile_id.description: Only tasks sent by this sender, by id from list_senders. Empty for everyone. (default: '')

record_id.description: Only this contact's tasks, by the id of their row in the sequence's audience table, which read_table_rows reads: how the Preview finds the card waiting on the contact on screen. The queue itself applies it, so it reaches every task. Empty for everyone. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

task_types.description: Only tasks of these types, which is how 'only the pending connection requests' is read: email, or a LinkedIn step (profile_view, connection_request, send_message, inmail, withdraw_connection_request, follow_contact, like_latest_post), or needs_human, a Browser use run that ended on Needs human. A connection request's Check whether they accepted is a profile_view. The queue itself applies it, before any filter this tool applies, so it reaches every task. Empty for every type. (maxItems: 9)

waiting_longer_than_days.description: Only tasks that have been in the queue longer than this many days, which is the answer to 'what is going stale'. Measured from when the task arrived, not from when its channel would run it.

to.description: Only tasks going to this recipient, matched as part of the contact's name, address, LinkedIn profile or domain in any case, so 'Melanie', 'melanie@acme.com' and 'acme.com' all work. Applied here rather than by the queue, over at most the first 50 tasks this reading returns in its order, and the answer says how many matched out of how many were read; search reaches every task. Empty for everybody. (maxLength: 320; default: '')

not_to.description: Leave out tasks going to this recipient, matched the same way as to. This is how 'approve all of them except the one to Melanie' is done: list with not_to 'Melanie', then approve the ids that come back. It also reads at most the first 50 tasks. Empty leaves nobody out. (maxLength: 320; default: '')

ask_reason.description: Only tasks held for a person for one of these reasons, which is how 'what was the agent unsure of' (low_confidence) or 'what did the checks catch' (findings, policy) is read: the Tasks page's Why it needs approval. Each row says its reason in words under held_because. The queue itself applies it, so it reaches every task. Empty for every reason. (maxItems: 28)

search.description: Words that must each appear in the contact's name, their email address or LinkedIn profile, or the message's subject, in any case: the Tasks page's search box ('the tasks about pricing', 'the ones to dana@acme.com'). It reads nothing else, not the contact's company, the sequence or the message's words, so a company is found only through addresses at its domain ('acme.com'). The queue itself applies it, so it reaches every task. Empty for every task. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

min_confidence.description: Only messages the agent scored itself at least this sure of, from 1 to 100. A task the agent did not write has no score, so any confidence filter leaves it out. Applied here like to, over at most the first 50 tasks.

max_confidence.description: Only messages the agent scored itself at most this sure of, from 1 to 100, which is how the shakiest drafts are found. Applied the same way as min_confidence.

order.description: The order to read them in, as the Tasks page's columns sort: newest_first (the default, the order the page opens in), oldest_first (the longest waiting on top), or contact_a_to_z and contact_z_to_a (the Contact column, each contact as it shows them: a LinkedIn profile by its handle, a task about nobody first A to Z). A filter applied here reads the first tasks in this order. (default: 'newest_first')

limit.description: How many rows to read, up to 50. With any filter applied here set, it caps the rows that matched instead. (minimum: 1; maximum: 50; default: 25)

tools.name: get_approval_task
tools.description: Read one task whole: the message exactly as it would send, subject and all (for a reply in an existing thread, the Re: subject it goes out with), the contact behind the label with their title and company, the sequence and step it belongs to, who decided it and what they wrote, and the approval rule that governs it. For a message the agent wrote it also gives the agent's confidence and its reason for it, why it waits, and what the checks found in it. Once approved it says where the work stands (queued and when it is expected to start, running, waiting for the sending window to open in its sender's timezone, paused until its sequence or contact is resumed, sent, or failed with why and whether its contact can be retried); while pending, whether its sequence is paused. An email card also lists the follow-ups the agent drafted with it, each with its step id and words: approving the card approves them too. It says what the send adds below the words, the sender's signature and the opt-out footer, and once the email went, its HTML part exactly as it left. Use it before approving anything a person should see the words of. A task that is already settled reads back the same way, with the rule as it stands NOW, because the product keeps no record of the rule that applied at the time and this will not invent one. Free.

tools.name: approve_tasks
tools.description: Let pending tasks run: an approved email sends within seconds, or when its sequence's sending window opens, and the follow-ups the agent drafted with it (get_approval_task lists them) are approved with it, each sent as written when its turn comes with no card of its own; an approved LinkedIn step joins its sender's line and runs in their browser, one at a time at the sender's Time between steps. A task whose sequence or contact is paused is approved all the same, but nothing of a paused sequence is sent: its approved step waits, in no line, until Resume sequence, and runs then. The answer says when, which is how 'approve them and tell me when they go out' is done: per sender, when the first and last LinkedIn step are expected to start, how many wait for the daily limit to reset (midnight in the sender's timezone), whether they wait for their sequence's sending window and when it opens, how many wait for a paused sequence or contact, and what stops them (no browser open, a limit); and whether the emails go now, when the window opens, or after Resume sequence. This REACHES PEOPLE OUTSIDE the workspace and cannot be undone, so it always asks a person first, whatever is allowed. Approve one task or up to 200 in one call; a task somebody has already decided is skipped and counted rather than failing the rest, and so is a LinkedIn step whose sender's LinkedIn is not connected, which keeps waiting until it is and is approved again, and a Needs human task, which nobody approves (mark_tasks_done is its tool). Its card names every task it lets go, with who it reaches and the start of what it says, any sender with no browser open and any paused sequence, and prices the sends: an email send and each LinkedIn step cost what the channel charges when it runs. It cannot change what a task says: rewrite_task_message does that first. It records no rating: approving from a list is not a verdict on each message, so the agent learns nothing new from it; but a task rewritten by Needs work, or edited by a person (its own email or one of the follow-ups it covers), carries the learning proposed on it, and a person approving it saves that learning (Approve plays the card's Save; an approval through an API key drops it instead), which writes again the messages written ahead that it reaches, free: at most 5 a channel of its sequence, or at most 5 across the workspace for one for all sequences (the answer says how many). It is refused while the rewrite is still being written. Set dry_run to check how many would go without approving or sending any.

task_ids.description: The tasks to decide, by id from list_approval_queue, up to 200 at once. A task somebody has already decided is skipped rather than failing the rest. (maxItems: 200)

dry_run.description: True checks how many of these tasks would go and changes nothing: no card, nothing sent. Leave it false to approve them. (default: False)

tools.name: reject_tasks
tools.description: Reject is about the person: this contact should not hear from the sequence, so it stops them. A complaint about the words is Needs work (mark_needs_work, with the task_id and the person's reason), never a rejection: it writes the words again instead of stopping anybody. A rejection teaches the agent nothing (a learning proposed on the task or on a follow-up it covers is dropped), and any note the person gave about the person is kept on every row it settles. READ THIS BEFORE USING IT: a rejection is a judgement about the CONTACT, not about this one step. The engine stops each of those contacts in their sequence on its next sweep, so the steps after this one do not send either, and nothing here restarts them; the Tasks page asks 'Stop writing to {name}?' for the same reason. A task that belongs to no sequence, or a Needs human task (mark_tasks_done is its tool), is only skipped. If somebody only wants this message changed, rewrite_task_message is the tool. If they want the person never contacted again by anything, this is not enough: add_to_do_not_contact is. Nothing is sent. Set dry_run to check how many would be refused without refusing any.

task_ids.description: The tasks to decide, by id from list_approval_queue, up to 200 at once. A task somebody has already decided is skipped rather than failing the rest. (maxItems: 200)

dry_run.description: True checks how many of these tasks would be refused and changes nothing: no card. Leave it false to refuse them. (default: False)

reason.description: A note about the person, only when they gave one ('wrong person', 'already a customer'), kept on every row it settles; never about the writing, which is mark_needs_work. Leave it empty when they gave none: the Tasks page sends none. (maxLength: 2000; default: '')

tools.name: rewrite_task_message
tools.description: Change what a pending task will send, before anybody approves it. The text REPLACES the draft whole, already rendered, so send the entire message rather than a note on what to change or a patch: when the person only said what to change ('shorter'), write the new words out whole here. An email may take a new subject; a LinkedIn note or message is clipped to LinkedIn's own ceilings exactly as the step's render would clip it. For a signed in person, your edit is kept; a learning is proposed from what changed, saved only when the person saves it. On an email card, follow_up_step_id rewrites one of the follow-ups it covers instead (get_approval_task lists them), and the others stay as they are. It works only while the task is pending: once the channel has it, the words a person saw are the words that send. NOTHING IS SENT by rewriting; approve_tasks is what sends.

task_id.description: The pending task to rewrite, from list_approval_queue.

body.description: The message as it should now send, whole. It REPLACES the drafted message rather than being added to it, so send the entire text, already rendered: nothing here fills in a merge field. (minLength: 1; maxLength: 50000)

subject.description: A new subject line for an email task. Leave it empty to keep the subject the task already carries. It cannot clear a subject, and a LinkedIn task has none to set. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

follow_up_step_id.description: To rewrite one of the follow-ups an email card covers instead of its own email: that follow-up's step id, from get_approval_task. Leave it empty to rewrite the card's own email. (default: '')

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.description: Read what came back: the replies sitting in the shared inbox, as summaries, or everything that went out. all holds what waits on us: a reply with no answer yet, an unread one, one whose reminder went off, or one we answered that went three business days unanswered (unless the label on their latest reply, set by the AI or a person, says it is over); one we answered moves to sent until then, and one marked done stays out until a new message reaches us. A search reads past that: every conversation the contact answered, waiting or not; a label lists every conversation carrying it. So reply_state replied on all lists only the ones back unanswered, and every conversation we answered is view sent with reply_state replied. sent holds every conversation we sent something in, a sequence step or a reply, on email or LinkedIn, answered or not and whatever became of it since, so a send nobody answered is found there (a LinkedIn reply still queued for the browser has not gone out). Choose a view: all, unread, needs_approval (a drafted reply waits for a person), needs_you (all that waits on a person: needs_approval's, rows marked needs_person, and open privacy requests), unlabelled (the work queue, real replies nobody has described yet), bounces, snoozed, sent, or all_mail: every conversation whatever became of it, so one marked done is found there. Away notices are labeled Out of office and other machine replies Auto-reply; both stay out of the Inbox until the contact writes, save one that came after a reply of theirs nobody answered. unread_only keeps the unread ones of any view, as the page's Unread switch does; the view unread is the same over all. Narrow it by label, by mailbox, by sequence, by sender, by channel, by whether we answered their latest reply (reply_state: replied, or not_replied for the ones still waiting on us), by free text over every message, and by a since and until day range, and leave out mailboxes, sequences or senders ('everything except Q3'). Sort by newest, by longest_waiting (the reply that has sat unanswered longest), by positives_first, or grouped by sequence. A long list comes a page at a time: the answer ends with the cursor that reads the next page. Every answer carries the unread count for the whole inbox. The labels are outcome labels and the seeded ones are Positive, Negative, Meeting booked, Meeting completed, Closed, Wrong contact, Out of office, Auto-reply. A row marked unsaved_feedback is the page's Unsaved feedback: notes on its waiting reply whose changes wait, saved by approve_and_send_draft and dropped by discard_draft_reply. A row's feedback is its feedback chip as the page shows it: Working on feedback (a note is read, or the words written again from one), Unsaved feedback or Saved feedback. It moves on by itself. A conversation's chip is read over its sent messages and its replies. THIS IS SUMMARIES ONLY: one line of the newest message each, never the conversation. read_conversation opens one and reads its messages; draft_reply writes an answer for a person to approve. It sends nothing and changes nothing.

view.description: all: what waits on us; unread: all, unread only; needs_approval: a draft waits; needs_you: waits on a person; unlabelled: nobody labeled it; bounces: failed deliveries; snoozed: until its reminder; sent: every one we sent in; all_mail: every one, done included. Away notices: label Out of office. (default: 'all')

unread_only.description: Only unread ones, in any view. (default: False)

search.description: Free text over messages and contact, best first, in or out of the Inbox. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

label.description: Every one with this label, by name, waiting or not. (maxLength: 120; default: '')

sender_profile_id.description: Only this sender, by id from list_senders. (default: '')

not_mailbox_ids.description: Leave out these mailboxes, by id.

not_sequence_ids.description: Leave out these sequences, by id.

not_sender_ids.description: Leave out these senders, by id.

reply_state.description: replied: we answered their latest (in all, only those back unanswered; every one: view sent); not_replied: it waits on us. (default: '')

since.description: Newest message on or after, YYYY-MM-DD. (pattern: ^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})?$; default: '')

until.description: Newest message on or before, YYYY-MM-DD. (pattern: ^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})?$; default: '')

sort.description: longest_waiting: unanswered longest on top; positives_first: positive labels first; sequence: grouped by sequence. (default: 'newest')

limit.description: Rows to read, up to 50. (minimum: 1; maximum: 50; default: 25)

tools.name: read_conversation
tools.description: Open one conversation and read it: who it is with, what it is labeled, whether it is done, comes back to the Inbox on a day or came back with no answer, and its messages oldest first, each with its message id (what forward_reply takes), who wrote it, when, whether it went out or came in, and the text. A reply the agent wrote is marked as sent as it wrote it, or as edited by a person before it went; one an older release sent with nobody reviewing it is marked so too. An email that came from an address other than the contact's own is marked with that address: the contact on a second address, or someone answering for them, such as a colleague, so it is never reported as the contact's own words. An attachment is named with the path a signed in person downloads it from, and a picture the email shows in its text (one pasted into it) is marked as shown inside the message; the bytes themselves are not readable here. A message whose files are still being read from the mailbox says so: its attachments are listed once they are. A drafted reply on the conversation is shown too, with the draft id the approve, revise and discard tools take, and where it stands: waiting for approval, with what the agent asks a person and how long the contact has waited, sending, possibly sent while the mailbox is checked, or failed to send; and when the agent wrote none, why. Only the most recent messages are printed in full when a thread is long, and each is cut to its first two thousand characters. Free.

thread_id.description: The conversation's id, from a read_inbox row.

tools.name: mark_conversations_done
tools.description: Mark conversations done, taking them out of the Inbox, or with not_done take the mark off. Done holds until a new message reaches us: their reply brings a conversation back, and so does an answer of ours that then goes three business days unanswered; an auto-reply, a bounce or a forward does not. Reach for it when a person says they are done with a conversation, it needs nothing more, take it out of the inbox, or don't bring it back: one we answered otherwise comes back after three business days unanswered, unless the label on their latest reply, set by the AI or a person, says the conversation is over. It also cancels a reminder the conversation was snoozed until. Nothing is sent and nothing is deleted: All mail lists it, a search or its label still finds it, and it opens from a link. Up to 200 at a time. Set dry_run to count what it would mark without marking anything.

thread_ids.description: The conversations, by id from read_inbox. Up to 200 at once. (maxItems: 200)

not_done.description: True takes the done mark off instead. Leave false to mark them done. (default: False)

dry_run.description: True counts the conversations this would mark and changes nothing: no card. Leave it false to mark them. (default: False)

annotations.title: Mark conversations done, or take the mark off

tools.name: mark_do_not_contact
tools.description: Put the contact behind one conversation, or behind several with thread_ids, on the do not contact list and stop every live sequence reaching them. This is the Inbox's own Do not contact, and what somebody means by 'they asked to be removed', 'unsubscribe them' or 'stop emailing him' about anyone with a conversation in the Inbox: use it, not add_to_do_not_contact with their address, which leaves the conversation where it is. Call it with preview_only true FIRST to be told which sequences would stop: that call reads and changes nothing. The suppression covers every future sequence in the workspace, not just the one they replied to, and taking somebody back off the list is a person's job. Each conversation is marked done too, as the page does: out of the Inbox until a new message reaches us, still in All mail, messages kept. A contact with no email address, such as a LinkedIn only one, is not added to the list: only their current sequences stop, and a later sequence can still enrol them. Set dry_run, the same as preview_only, to learn what it would stop without suppressing anyone.

thread_id.description: The conversation whose contact is being suppressed, by id from read_inbox. (default: '')

thread_ids.description: Several conversations at once, up to 200, by id from read_inbox, for 'do not contact all of these'. Use it instead of thread_id, or with it. (maxItems: 200)

preview_only.description: True names the sequences this would stop and changes NOTHING, which is what to call first when somebody asks what would happen. False suppresses the contacts and stops those sequences. (default: False)

dry_run.description: The same as preview_only, by the name every removal shares: true names the sequences this would stop and changes nothing, no card. Either one makes the call a read. (default: False)

annotations.title: Add a contact to Do not contact

tools.name: list_reply_labels
tools.description: List the outcome labels this workspace has: what each is called, its color and icon, how many conversations carry it, whether it is one of the seeded ones, whether it counts into the positive reply rate, and whether its conversations wait outside the working views. The seeded ones are Positive, Negative, Meeting booked, Meeting completed, Closed, Wrong contact, Out of office, Auto-reply, they cannot be renamed, and they are the only labels the classifier ever applies by itself. Read this before labeling anything, since every labeling tool here works in names. Free.

tools.name: set_conversation_labels
tools.description: Change the labels one conversation carries, by name. add_labels and remove_labels change only the labels named and keep every other; labels makes it carry exactly that set instead, and the card shows what it carries now beside what it will; clear_labels takes every label off. A label that does not exist is refused with the real ones named, and a name two labels share is asked about; nothing here creates a label by accident. Labels are what the positive reply rate is counted from, so this changes reporting as well as which view the conversation sits in. A built-in label put on is the person's verdict on the conversation's latest reply, and replaces the built-in label the AI gave that reply, which comes off the conversation (so Positive put on a reply the AI read as Meeting booked takes Meeting booked off). The AI keeps the person's label: a label the sequence's agent writes replies for has it write one, any other retires its waiting draft, a reply that left the follow-ups going (an away notice, an auto-reply, a not now) stops them under any label but Out of office or Auto-reply, and Negative counts the stop as Said no.

thread_id.description: The conversation, by id from read_inbox.

add_labels.description: Labels to put on it, by name. Every label it already carries stays, except the built-in label the AI gave its latest reply, which a built-in label replaces. (maxItems: 50)

remove_labels.description: Labels to take off it, by name. Every other label stays. (maxItems: 50)

labels.description: Instead of adding and removing: the exact labels it should carry afterwards, by name, replacing what it carries. The card shows what it carries now beside what it will carry. (maxItems: 50)

clear_labels.description: True takes every label off it. Send nothing else with it. (default: False)

tools.name: draft_reply
tools.description: Write a reply to one conversation and leave it waiting for approval, with an optional one line steer saying what it should do. On a conversation from a sequence, that sequence's agent writes it, in its own voice and from what it knows about the contact, as the same reply it writes for every reply and charged as that reply: IT CAN SPEND CREDITS. Words the agent already wrote for the message cost nothing more; a steer, or a message the agent has not answered yet, has them written, which is charged at the agent's reply price. A conversation outside every sequence, or whose sequence is gone, has no agent, and is refused: its replies are written by hand. Say what it may cost before you call it for a person. IT SENDS NOTHING: the draft lands in Needs approval as editable text, and approve_and_send_draft is the only tool that sends it. Never tell anybody a reply went out because this succeeded. The writer sometimes declines rather than inventing filler, usually on an automatic message or a bounce, and the answer says so; a sequence with no audience set up is refused with the reason.

thread_id.description: The conversation to reply in, by id from read_inbox.

steer.description: One line telling the model what the reply should do: 'offer Tuesday or Thursday', 'thank them and close it out'. Leave empty to let it read the conversation and decide. (maxLength: 500; default: '')

tools.name: revise_draft
tools.description: Change a drafted reply, in one of two ways. Send body_text to EDIT it to exactly that text, keeping what was first written beside it for comparison; an edit costs nothing. On a reply a sequence's agent wrote, your edit is kept; a learning is proposed from what changed, saved only when the person sends it or saves it, and dismiss_proposed_learning drops it. Leave body_text empty to have it written again instead, the draft's Rewrite with no note, optionally told what to do differently; the superseded draft is kept. Writing it again is charged like draft_reply, as a plain rewrite (a rewrite after Needs work, mark_needs_work with draft_id, is free and teaches): the sequence's agent charges its reply turn again, and a conversation no longer in a sequence is refused, the draft left as it was. If nothing usable comes back, the old draft is gone all the same and nothing waits on the conversation. Whatever is written waits for a person, and NOTHING IS SENT. A reply that is sending, may already have sent, or failed to send is refused, as is one already sent or discarded.

draft_id.description: The draft, by id from read_conversation. (default: '')

body_text.description: The reply as it should now read, whole. Setting it EDITS the draft to exactly this text. Leave it empty to have the model write another one instead. (maxLength: 20000; default: '')

subject.description: A new subject line, when editing. Leave empty to keep the one it has. (maxLength: 500; default: '')

steer.description: One line saying what to do differently, used only when body_text is empty: 'shorter', 'do not offer a call yet'. (maxLength: 500; default: '')

tools.name: approve_and_send_draft
tools.description: Send a waiting draft as it stands. Pass the conversation's thread_id with the draft_id: the draft is checked first, and a reply that is sending, may already have sent, or failed to send is refused without a send being tried, because approving it could send the same words twice. THIS IS THE ONLY TOOL THAT SENDS A DRAFTED REPLY, and it reaches a person outside the workspace, so it always asks first however the workspace has set its permissions. It goes out the way the message it answers came in: by email from the mailbox that email reached, so the prospect sees it from the address they wrote to, or on LinkedIn when they answered there, whichever way the conversation began. It CANNOT BE TAKEN BACK. Read the draft first, and revise_draft it before approving if any word of it is wrong. A draft already sent or discarded is refused, and so is one that answers an older message while the contact's newer one waits, which keeps waiting until somebody reads that message, and one whose message was answered already from the mailbox, LinkedIn or here. Once it is sent the conversation leaves the Inbox for Sent, and the answer says the day it comes back if they stay quiet, or that the label on their latest reply closes it; mark_conversations_done keeps it out for good, snooze_conversations brings it back at another time. A reply rewritten by Needs work, or edited by a person, carries the learning proposed on it: sending it saves that learning, which writes again the messages written ahead that it reaches, free (the card says how many), and it is refused while the rewrite is still being written. Set dry_run to make every check the send makes without sending anything.

draft_id.description: The draft, by id from read_conversation. (default: '')

thread_id.description: The conversation the draft is on, by id from read_inbox. Send it: the draft is checked against what is waiting there first, and one that is sending or may already have sent is refused without a send being tried. (default: '')

contact_name.description: Who it goes to, so the approval card names a person rather than an id: the contact, or the colleague read_conversation says it goes to when one answered for them. Not sent anywhere. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

dry_run.description: True makes every check the send makes and sends nothing: no card. Leave it false to send it. (default: False)

without_file.description: Send it although its words say something is attached and no file goes with it. Only when the person said to; a send refused for that says so. (default: False)

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description: Read how many credits this workspace has left, what the plan grants each period, when it refills, how many of the credits left expire at the refill (a Free workspace's unspent monthly credits; paid, bought, and referral credits never expire), and whether credits are low or gone. Reach for it for 'how many credits do I have', 'am I about to run out', 'do my credits expire' and before proposing anything expensive. It also says how far back usage history can be read, which bounds every report in this family. It does NOT say what anything costs, which is get_pricing, and it does NOT say where the credits went, which is get_credit_spend. Free.

tools.name: get_business_context
tools.description: Read the seven business context fields every AI feature in this workspace writes from: Company description, Ideal customer profile, Ideal buyer personas, Interest signals, Social proof, Free offer, and Voice, the two choices beside them (Company type and Sells to) and the page the company description was last written from. Read this BEFORE writing any email, campaign, agent prompt or AI column about this company, and read it first whenever somebody says the AI has them wrong. It names the fields that are still empty, which is usually the answer. It does NOT include the reference documents, which list_reference_documents reads, and long fields are trimmed with the real length named. Free, and it changes nothing.

tools.name: update_business_context
tools.description: Write new text into one or more of the seven business context fields, or set Company type or Sells to (keep leaves either as it is). Each field sent REPLACES that field whole rather than being added to, so read it with get_business_context first and send the old text back along with the new when somebody is adding to it. A field left empty is untouched: to empty one, name it in clear_fields, which asks the person first because the text is not kept. The card shows each field as it is and as it would be, and a call that changes nothing is refused. This is the tool for 'we also sell to X', 'add this case study', 'stop saying we are a startup' and 'change our company voice' (we spell it the British way, we say members not customers); how bold or warm the emails sound goes in the sequence's message prompts instead. It will not touch the reference documents, and it does not rewrite anything already generated: every AI feature picks the new text up on its next run. Only a workspace admin can change the business context; a member is refused before any card. Never say is a list, changed with add_never_say and remove_never_say ('never say guaranteed ROI', 'don't mention Acme'): unlike Voice, which is advice, every message the agent writes is checked against it, in any language and in other words, written again without the phrase, then held in Tasks for a person. A phrase added also holds the messages already waiting to go out that say it (each needs Approve anyway); ask the person whether to leave them held or rewrite them (waiting), and never pick for them.

company_description.description: Company description: what the company does, in prose, the product, who it is for and how it is sold. Replaces the whole field. Empty leaves it.

ideal_customer_profile.description: Which COMPANIES are worth selling to: size, industry, how they buy, what makes one a good fit. Replaces the whole field.

ideal_buyer_personas.description: Which PEOPLE inside those companies to write to: their roles, what they care about, what they are measured on. Replaces the whole field.

interest_signals.description: What makes a company or a person worth reaching out to now: hiring, funding, a tool they use, something they said. Replaces the whole field.

social_proof.description: The customers, numbers and case studies an email may name. Replaces the whole field, so send every proof that should stay.

pilot_offer.description: Free offer: what the company's own website gives a new customer free to start (a free trial, plan, pilot, audit or sample), in a line. Only what the site or the person says they offer, never one you made up; empty when they offer nothing free. The Introduce your company sequence template ends on it, and asks for a short call while it is empty. Replaces the whole field.

voice.description: Voice: how the company words things, as properties rather than quotes. Its spelling, how formal it is, what it calls its product and its buyers, jargon it avoids. Every email the agent writes matches it. Not how bold or warm one sequence's emails sound, which goes in that sequence's message prompts. Replaces the whole field.

company_type.description: Company type, how the company makes money: keep (leave it), b2b_saas, b2c_saas, agency_services, ecommerce_dtc, marketplace, manufacturing, financial_services, healthcare, education, nonprofit, government, media_publishing, real_estate, hospitality, logistics or other. Descriptive: shown here and to AI apps, read by no writer yet. (default: 'keep')

sells_to.description: Sells to, who buys from the company: keep (leave it), businesses, consumers or both. Descriptive, like company_type. (default: 'keep')

add_never_say.description: Phrases or claims to add to Never say, the list no AI message may use ('guaranteed ROI', a client's name). Every message the agent writes is checked against it, in any language and in other words, written again without the phrase, then held in Tasks. Kept with the phrases already there. (maxItems: 100)

remove_never_say.description: Phrases to take off Never say, as the list prints them. Asks first. (maxItems: 100)

waiting.description: What happens to the messages already waiting to go out that a phrase added to Never say holds: keep or leave (the default: they stay held in Tasks, each needing Approve anyway, the page's Leave them) or rewrite (written again without the phrase now, free, at most 5 in the workspace, soonest sending first: Rewrite them). Ask the person which before adding a phrase; never pick for them. (default: 'keep')

clear_fields.description: The fields to EMPTY, by these names: company_description, ideal_customer_profile, ideal_buyer_personas, interest_signals, social_proof, pilot_offer, voice, company_type, sells_to. The only way to empty one: a field left empty above is kept as it is. Emptying asks the person first, because the text there is not kept anywhere. (maxItems: 9)

tools.name: write_business_context_from_website
tools.description: Read the workspace's own company website and write the business context from what it says: the written fields (the Free offer among them, left empty when the site offers nothing free), Company type and Sells to. It reads up to 18 pages of the site, the company's LinkedIn page, what other sites say about it and the reference documents, and leaves a field empty when nothing read backs it. Reach for it for a workspace whose context is empty, or when somebody asks to write it from their site. It is for this workspace's own company: to research other companies, add the Company researcher agent to a table. With a domain it REPLACES those fields, including anything somebody wrote by hand (all but a Free offer a person wrote, which it keeps), so read them first and say what is about to be overwritten: that call always asks the person, and its card shows the text it replaces. With no domain it uses the domain in the signed in person's email address, and that only writes anything for the person who created the workspace, when every field is still empty and no run has happened before, which it says plainly rather than pretending to have worked; when that address is a personal one (gmail, outlook) or it wrote nothing, ask the person for their company website and pass it as the domain. When the business context is empty, offer this BEFORE adding an AI column, a built-in agent or emails that read it, and once it is approved carry on with what was asked in the same turn, but run nothing that reads the business context until get_business_context shows text in it. A run takes up to about 3 minutes. It starts the run and waits about a minute; a run still going after that is handed back by id with how far it got and carries on, and only one may run at a time. It spends no credits, and a site with little public text produces little. With a domain only a workspace admin can start it. One company per business context: a domain other than the website it was written from is refused before any card with the question to ask the person ("Rewrite your business context for X instead of Y?"); call again with replace_other_company only once they say yes. That keeps the earlier company for 30 days, which restore_previous_business_context puts back.

domain.description: The company website to read, like acme.com (a full address is read down to its domain). Leave it empty to use the domain in the signed in person's email address, which only writes anything when every field is still empty and no run has happened before. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

replace_other_company.description: True only once the person said yes to rewriting a business context written from ANOTHER website than domain: one company per business context, or every AI message mixes both. Without it such a call is refused before any card, with the question to ask. The earlier company is kept for 30 days, and restore_previous_business_context puts it back. (default: False)

annotations.title: Write the business context from a website

tools.name: list_reference_documents
tools.description: List the documents attached to the business context, oldest first, with what each one's summary says and whether any prompt actually reads it. Three things here are only visible on this listing: a document still being read, a document switched off, and a document whose summary sits past the prompt budget and so is read by nothing however much it says. Free, and it changes nothing. It cannot attach a file: an upload happens on the Reference documents tab, and add_reference_documents_from_drive takes files picked in Google Drive.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List the tools this workspace has connected, worst health first, with the type of each, whether it is still working and what kinds of record it handles. Start here for anything about an integration: every other tool in this family takes a name or an id from this list. The health shown is the LAST check rather than a live one, so an old check proves nothing about right now; check_connections_now asks the providers. Free, and it changes nothing.

search.description: Only connections whose name or type carries these words. Leave empty for everything connected. (maxLength: 255; default: '')

kind.description: Whether the connection can be read from (source), written to (destination), or either way (both). 'any' does not narrow at all, and is almost always what a person means. (default: 'any')

record_types.description: Only connections that handle any of these kinds of record, as the slugs list_connection_record_types reports, for example person or companies. A slug nothing recognizes is ignored rather than refused. (maxItems: 20)

limit.description: How many connections to print, worst health first. (minimum: 1; maximum: 50; default: 25)

tools.name: search_playbooks
tools.description: Find maintained guidance before substantial strategy, designing a new sequence, industry openers or optimization advice (targeting, cadence, conversions, table research, agent learnings). Not for a change the person has fully specified or a correction of an earlier proposal: follow their latest instruction. In a mixed request, search only the undecided part. Include the audience, relationship and open question; use English search terms even when answering in another language. Returns up to three excerpts and IDs for read_playbook. This reads guidance, not live workspace state.

tools.name: read_playbook
tools.description: Read a complete outreach or Oneprofile workflow playbook by the ID returned by search_playbooks, including sources, evidence limits and review date. Read the relevant chapters before advising, and check applicability first. Never use a template to override specified changes. Product tools and current help remain the authority on supported actions and prices; sample openers require verified facts before they can be used for a contact.

tools.name: mark_needs_work
tools.description: Needs work: tell an agent what is wrong with something it wrote, in the person's words. It proposes learnings from the reason (or rewrites of the ones about the same thing) and writes that output again with them, as the page's Needs work does: cells of an agent column are run again, a Preview example is run again, a task's message, a contact's messages in a sequence's Preview or a step's Preview, and a reply it drafted are written again in place, and a message that already went out is not resent: the agent writes what it would have sent instead (read_needs_work). Nothing is saved until the page's yes: approving the task, sending the reply, or Looks good (save_proposed_learning does the same; on a sequence for this sequence unless switched; on a table agent its own), and leaving it saves nothing. A second Needs work on the same message, cells of the same column or Preview example, or thumbs_down_id with the person's reason, is a further note in its feedback (the latest note wins): it sharpens the waiting changes, and on a learning proposed from an edit it rewrites nothing. The answer lists each change with its change_id, for edit_feedback_change. Words a person edited are refused: their edit proposes its own learning. Reject on a task is about the person, never the words: a complaint about the words is Needs work. Name exactly one thing. A complaint about a whole sequence's messages with no step named ('these are too salesy, fix it', 'make them bolder') is this too, on ONE contact: take a contact_id from read_sequence_previews, or write_sequence_previews when none is written, and pass the person's words as the reason. Say above the card that it rewrites only that contact and that Looks good saves the learning for every contact. Never edit_message_prompts for it. With nobody to write for (no audience, or nobody the sequence can reach), say so and offer add_agent_learning on that sequence in the person's words. A step a person wrote has no agent to teach: edit_sequence_steps changes its words. Never write the reason yourself: with none, ask the person why. On a sequence's message the rewrite is free: a workspace has 100 free rewrites a day, and past them Needs work is refused until they reset; the refusal says when. On a table agent every note's redo costs what the page's Needs work box says; with no credits left the redo is refused and the session still waits. undo_needs_work is Discard feedback: every change is dropped and the earlier output put back. For another version with no learning, use the plain write-again tool of the family that owns the output instead, which is charged.

reason.description: What is wrong, in the person's own words: the agent learns its rule from them. Never write one yourself. When the person has not said why, ask them first. (maxLength: 1000; default: '')

table_id.description: Cells: the table, by the id from list_tables, with column and row_ids. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

column.description: Cells: the agent column, by its name on the table or its id. (maxLength: 200; default: '')

row_ids.description: Cells: the rows whose cell needs work, from read_table_rows, at most 50. (maxItems: 50)

task_id.description: A task's message: the task, from list_approval_queue. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

draft_id.description: A reply the agent drafted on the Inbox, from read_conversation. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

agent.description: A Preview example: the saved agent, by its name or id, with example_id. (maxLength: 200; default: '')

example_id.description: A Preview example: the example's id, as the agent's Preview printed it. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

sequence.description: A contact's messages in a sequence's Preview: the sequence, by name or id. (maxLength: 200; default: '')

contact_id.description: With sequence: the contact, by the contact_id check_outbound_writing, read_sequence_previews, write_sequence_previews or preview_outbound_message printed beside them. Their messages must be written: one only the Builder wrote joins the open Preview first, as it is. Nothing written yet and words a person edited are refused. An email that already went out takes message_id instead. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

message_id.description: A message or reply the agent wrote that already went out, by the id read_outbound_conversation printed beside it, the mark_needs_work message_id read_conversation prints beside it in the Inbox (never the Inbox's own message id), or the message_id list_sender_activity prints on a row. It is not sent again: the agent writes its next ones with the learning. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

thumbs_down_id.description: Feedback waiting to be saved, from list_agent_learnings or the answer that proposed it. Needs work on it is a further note in the same session (the latest note wins): the reason sharpens its changes; on a table agent's cells or Preview example it runs them again, priced as the first note was; on a learning proposed from an edit it rewrites nothing. (maxLength: 64; default: '')

annotations.title: Mark what an agent wrote as Needs work

tools.name: get_first_sequence
tools.description: Read where the workspace's first sequence stands: the sequence the setup wizard builds from the company's website, in its five steps (Research your company, Choose who to reach, Find people, Review the messages, Connect your mailbox). Says the step it is at and which tool goes on, with the link that opens that step on the setup page, where Continue with Google and start sending connects the mailbox and starts it. Once launched, says whether it is sending or paused. With wait it waits up to a minute for the next step to land. Free.

wait.description: Wait up to a minute for the next step to land (the audiences, the people, the first emails) before answering. (default: False)

tools.name: start_first_sequence
tools.description: Set up a new workspace's first sequence from the company's website, as the setup wizard after sign-up does: it finds up to 100 people who fit the ideal customer profile and writes each a personal sequence, as many as the workspace's credits cover, and the person starts it from their own mailbox on the setup page. This call reads the website into the business context and suggests audiences (buyers by job title and company); pick_first_sequence_audience then finds and writes to the people of one. With no website named it looks up the one the sign-in email names, to confirm. Waits up to a minute for the audiences. This call is free. Only the person who created the workspace may start it; refused for a personal mail domain, while another website's research runs, and past three companies a day. A website other than the one the business context was written from is refused until replace_business_context is set, which rewrites what the workspace says it sells. One is set up at a time: when one is already being set up, says where it stands instead, unless its website could not be read or another website is named before its people are found: then it starts over.

domain.description: The company's website, like acme.com, as the person confirmed it. Empty starts nothing: it answers the domain of their sign-in address to confirm with them first (a personal address like gmail.com names none: ask for the website). (maxLength: 255; default: '')

replace_business_context.description: Only once the person said yes to rewriting a business context written from another website. (default: False)

description.description: Only when reading the website failed: what the company sells and who buys it, in the person's own two sentences. The audiences are written from it and the site is not read again. (maxLength: 600; default: '')

tools.name: pick_first_sequence_audience
tools.description: Pick the audience of the workspace's first sequence, by its number on get_first_sequence: finds up to 100 people of it, researches the first five (work email, why them) and writes their first messages, waiting up to a minute for them. The rest are researched once it starts, from the workspace's own credits, as far as they cover: the answer says how many. A pick stands once people are found; with switch it finds new people for another audience and writes to five, removing the people and messages of the one before. Refused for an audience matching under 50 people.

number.description: The audience's number, as get_first_sequence lists it: [1] is 1. (minimum: 1)

switch.description: Replace an audience already picked with this one: its people and emails are removed and this one's are found and written. (default: False)

tools.name: remove_first_sequence_people
tools.description: Take people out of the first sequence before it launches: by their full name as get_first_sequence lists them (a duplicate, a junk record), and everyone at the companies named (current customers, open deals), by domain or name. A domain also goes on the workspace's do-not-contact list, so no sequence writes there. Someone whose messages are written is skipped, so nothing written for them sends. Free. Refused once the sequence has launched. Set dry_run to count who would leave without taking anyone out.

people.description: People to take out, by their full name as get_first_sequence lists it. (maxItems: 100)

companies.description: Companies whose people all leave, such as current customers or open deals: a domain (acme.com, also put on the workspace's do-not-contact list) or a name. (maxItems: 100)

dry_run.description: True counts who would leave, through every check, and takes nobody out: no card. Leave it false to take them out. (default: False)

annotations.title: Take people out of the first sequence

tools.name: reshape_first_sequence_audience
tools.description: Set where one offered audience's people are (countries or regions, up to five; empty for anywhere) and how big their companies are (fewest and most employees), by its number on get_first_sequence, then count it again, waiting up to a minute for the count. For a person who sells into another region or company size than the audiences offered. Free. Refused once an audience is picked.

number.description: The audience's number, as get_first_sequence lists it: [1] is 1. (minimum: 1)

locations.description: The countries or regions its people are in, such as Germany or Europe; empty for anywhere. Replaces the places it had. (maxItems: 5)

headcount_min.description: The fewest employees at their companies; 0 for no floor. (minimum: 0; default: 0)

headcount_max.description: The most employees at their companies; 0 for no ceiling. (minimum: 0; default: 0)

annotations.title: Change the first sequence's region or company size

tools.name: choose_first_sequence_business_line
tools.description: For a company that runs several businesses (get_first_sequence lists its business lines and says when to ask): say which one the person sells for, or empty for the whole company. The Business context is narrowed to it and three audiences are written for it in place of the ones before, waiting up to a minute for them. Free. Refused once an audience is picked.

line.description: One of the business lines get_first_sequence lists, word for word, as the person named it; empty for the whole company. (maxLength: 60; default: '')

annotations.title: Choose what the first sequence sells

tools.name: set_first_sequence_sender
tools.description: Set who signs the emails of the workspace's first sequence (the one the setup wizard builds): the person's name and, if they give one, title. A sign-up with only an email has no name, so its emails end with the company's name until this is set; get_first_sequence says when. The written emails are signed again at once, nothing is rewritten. Also sets the meeting link the emails that ask for a meeting offer, as Connect your mailbox asks for it. Free. Refused once the sequence has started.

name.description: The person's full name, as the emails are signed: Ada Lovelace. (minLength: 1; maxLength: 120)

title.description: Their job title under the name, like Founder. Left out keeps the one there.

meeting_link.description: Their booking page, like https://cal.com/ada, offered in the emails that ask for a meeting. Left out keeps the one there.

clear_meeting_link.description: True takes the meeting link away. (default: False)

tools.name: approve_first_sequence_emails
tools.description: Mark a person's first emails Looks good in the workspace's first sequence (the one the setup wizard builds), once the person says they look good: the Looks good of the setup page. These are what send, what the feedback proposed is saved, and the setup page goes on to Connect your mailbox. Name the email by the number get_first_sequence shows before it. Free.

person.description: The number get_first_sequence shows before the email: [1] is 1. (minimum: 1; maximum: 100; default: 1)

annotations.title: Mark the first emails as good to send

tools.name: show_first_sequence_steps
tools.description: Write and show every step of one person's sequence in the workspace's first sequence (the one the setup wizard builds): the follow-up emails and LinkedIn messages, not only the first ones, so the person reads what sends before they launch. The setup page's Show every step. Also says where each claim in the first email came from (their row, research on them, the website, only the feedback) and which nothing backs, and the learnings that state what the website does not, as the setup page marks them before launch. Name the email by the number get_first_sequence shows before it. Free: the follow-ups it writes are kept in the first sequence, as the page's are.

person.description: The number get_first_sequence shows before the email: [1] is 1. (minimum: 1; maximum: 100; default: 1)

tools.name: edit_first_sequence_email
tools.description: Edit a first email of the workspace's first sequence (the one the setup wizard builds) by hand, as the setup page's Edit does: the words given send to that person as written, the signature added below. For a small exact change the person spells out (fix a word, drop a sentence); for a change in tone or approach, give_first_sequence_feedback teaches the agent instead. Name the email by the number get_first_sequence shows before it. Free. Refused once the sequence has started.

person.description: The number get_first_sequence shows before the email: [1] is 1. (minimum: 1; maximum: 100)

body.description: The whole email as it should send, without the signature: it is added below. The words get_first_sequence shows, with only the person's change made. (minLength: 1; maxLength: 5000)

subject.description: The subject; left out keeps the one written.

tools.name: give_first_sequence_feedback
tools.description: Give feedback on a first email of the workspace's first sequence (the one the setup wizard builds), in the person's own words: the agent learns from it and writes that person's email again, and keeps doing it for the rest. Name the email by the number get_first_sequence shows before it. Waits up to a minute (less from an AI app) for the new words; if they are not ready, get_first_sequence shows them. Free.

note.description: What to change, in the person's own words: shorter, mention our free trial, less formal. (minLength: 1; maxLength: 1000)

person.description: The number get_first_sequence shows before the email: [1] is 1. (minimum: 1; maximum: 100; default: 1)

annotations.title: Give feedback on the first emails
